description: No person-level official feed links a named individual to an approved role at a named regulated CZ entity; the join must be reconstructed from entity registers plus commercial-register officer changes.

ČNB open data covers only seven datasets (banks, exchange offices, consumer-credit providers and intermediaries) — payment institutions, e-money institutions and small-scale providers appear only via JERRS/WS JERRS, not as plain CSV.
Sector self-regulatory and professional bodies adjacent to the statutory regulators (Česká bankovní asociace, Česká asociace pro platební styk / fintech associations) were not scouted in this cell.

English-language ČNB mirrors were confirmed for press releases and payments licensing, but it was not established whether the registers, open data and final-decision listings have equivalent en versions.
No historical/archived snapshots of the CZ registers were identified, so back-testing leadership-change detection over past years is not currently possible from official sources.

Cell list omits several relevant CZ deposit-takers and specialised banks whose leadership moves matter to the same market map: Hypoteční banka, ČSOB Stavební spořitelna, Modrá pyramida (KB group), Stavební spořitelna České spořitelny, Max banka, mBank CZ branch, ING CZ, J&T Banka, PPF banka, Wüstenrot.

This cell is newsroom-only by design, so it cannot see leadership changes that are legally registered but never announced (obchodní rejstřík / justice.cz filings of statutory-body changes, ČNB's list of licensed persons and management approvals).
Newsrooms cover appointments well but rarely cover ordinary hiring volume, team build-outs, or layoffs. The 'jobs/hiring' topic is therefore under-served by this cell.

English-language mirrors exist for several issuers (fio.cz/about-us/media/press-releases, unicreditbank.cz/en/, csob.cz EN portal) but were not systematically enumerated; EN mirrors sometimes lag or omit local appointment releases.

No liveness or robots/ToS check was performed on any listed URL in this pass, and some portal URLs (ČSOB Liferay asset_publisher links) are query-parameter heavy and may not be stable canonical addresses.
Municipal and regional (obce, kraje, městské části) buyers of payment/acquiring services are unrepresented.
Audit and oversight bodies (NKÚ, Úřad pro ochranu hospodářské soutěže / ÚOHS decisions on procurement challenges) not covered.
The supplier ecosystem revealed by contract awards (acquirers, processors, systems integrators) has no dedicated source yet — only the registers that name them.
English-language coverage of this cell is thin: only TED was captured in en, and no en-language reporting on Czech state payments procurement.
No URL in this slice was fetched; all endpoints are search-derived and unverified.
Accenture CZ, PwC CZ and IBM/NCR Atleos CZ were not covered with dedicated local-language sources; PwC in particular was not searched at all in this slice.

Vendor-side job postings — the most direct A5 signal in this cell — remain uncollected. Careers pages of Trask, Aricoma/Cleverlance, Asseco CE, Monet+, ArnaThora, Loomis CZ and G4S CZ were identified as targets but not enumerated.

Czech commercial-register sources (ARES / justice.cz / or.justice.cz Sbírka listin) were not exercised, though they give vendor headcount, revenue and statutory-body changes for CZ subsidiaries of every actor in this cell.
ICZ, KB SmartSolutions, Adastra, GEM System, Komix and other mid-tier CZ bank integrators were not reached within this slice's query budget.
Most located personnel evidence dates to 2025 or earlier; no 2026 vendor FS-leadership appointments were confirmed in this run.

Only Zlatá koruna (/soutez/{YEAR} back to ~2009) and ČNB were confirmed to expose a deep, systematically addressable past-edition archive. For most conference sites in this cell the archive depth was not established.
Almost every source found is Prague-centred, with Brno appearing only via FinTech Roadmap's earlier editions. No Ostrava/Brno/Plzeň regional banking or payments event was identified.

Card schemes, acquirers, PSPs and POS/terminal vendors are only indirectly represented (via Mastercard at Banka roku and Economia's card conference). No dedicated CZ acquiring/merchant-services event was found.

The glossary built during this run covers award/jury and speaker terminology (porota, odborná porota, přednášející, řečníci, panelisté, medailonky diskutujících, ročník, program) but the title-normalisation vocabulary for CZ banking roles was only partially exercised.

University-industry coverage rests almost entirely on VŠE Praha. Other CZ finance faculties (Masarykova univerzita ESF, VŠB-TU Ostrava, Univerzita Karlova IES) were not searched for industry panels or career-day rosters.

No URL in this slice has been verified for liveness; several were derived from search-result summaries rather than direct fetch. Only zlatakoruna.info and paymentsummit.cz were fetched directly during this run.

No per-bank union organisation website or newsletter was located for the big three (Česká spořitelna, ČSOB, Komerční banka). ZO entities are confirmed to exist as registered legal persons (multiple IČOs each) and OSPPP has per-employer subpages, but their own communication channels (intranet-only in many cases) were not found.

This slice is bank-heavy. Payments-specific employers (payment institutions, card processors, fintechs, shared-service/offshoring centres run by banking groups in Brno/Ostrava) were not separately searched for workforce/union coverage.

No FOI-style collection path was tested. The Czech Freedom of Information Act (zákon č. 106/1999 Sb.) could compel Úřad práce ČR to disclose mass-redundancy notifications by NACE sector and possibly by employer.
English-language coverage of this cell is thin and mostly EU-level (Eurofound ERM, UNI Europa). No Czech-based English-language outlet covering bank labour disputes was identified.
ČNB branch-count data was confirmed to exist and be cited by media, but the exact ARAD time-series identifier for branch / business-place counts was not pinned down in this pass.
Only three kraj-level media markets (MS, Jihomoravský, Královéhradecký) are represented; ten remain unmapped.
Czech-language standalone discussion forums (non-Reddit) are entirely absent from the candidate set.
Atmoskop employer IDs were resolved for only one banking group (Česká spořitelna and its pension subsidiary); the rest of the CZ bank/payment-institution roster is unmapped.
No union or works-council source was found, though collective-bargaining bodies (e.g. banking-sector trade unions) publish reorganisation and redundancy news earlier than employers.
Regional labour-office (Úřad práce) statistics and mass-layoff notifications by kraj were not covered, yet they are the authoritative record of hromadné propouštění.
Job-board and review sources give point-in-time snapshots only; nothing in the set preserves history.
No verified, collectable Reuters/Bloomberg pathway for CZ banking leadership news.

The Wayback/archive capability is identified but no concrete watchlist of CZ leadership URLs to snapshot and diff has been built (csob.cz, csas.cz, kb.cz, rb.cz, moneta.cz, airbank.cz, comgate.cz management pages).

International English trackers found here skew to banks and their parents; CZ payments-specific actors (Comgate, GoPay, Global Payments CZ, Worldline CEE, Mastercard/Visa CZ country managers) are barely covered.
This cell's international trackers cover senior leadership moves well but give almost nothing on the 'jobs/hiring' topic (headcount, recruitment volumes, layoffs) for CZ banking.
Several of the highest-value English sources for this cell (bne IntelliNews, Central Banking, Euromoney, The Official Board, GlobalData) are subscription-gated.
ATM/terminal estate operators (Euronet CZ, Diebold Nixdorf s.r.o., NCR Voyix/Atos country teams) have no identified direct announcement channel.
Card schemes' CZ offices (Visa CZ, Mastercard Europe CZ) unscouted in this slice.
Comgate's own corporate website / press section was not directly located; only its LinkedIn and an encyclopedic entry surfaced.
No executive-search / HR-recruiter channel scouted (specialised fintech recruiters often announce placed country managers).
Most corroborating articles surfaced are 2024-2025 vintage; current-year (2026) leadership state is unverified.
No licensed full-text access to the paywalled Czech business press (HN, Ekonom, Deník N, parts of E15/Euro), which is where forced exits and restructuring rationales are actually explained.

Coverage found is heavily Prague/national-outlet centric. Regional Czech business press (Deník regional titles, Moravskoslezský/Brno business media) was not probed, so branch-network closures and regional bank hiring may be under-detected.

This slice built source coverage but not yet a complete CZ banking/payments actor map (banks, ČNB, ČBA, payment institutions, fintechs, and their alias/inflected Czech forms) to filter the generalist people-moves columns.
Payments-specific press (acquirers, card schemes, PSPs, POS/terminal vendors) is not represented; all sources found skew to banks and insurers.

Back-catalogue depth of the personalia columns (how far Newstream /stitek/personalie, Bankovnictví /personalie and Měšec /n/personalie paginate) was not measured, so historical backfill feasibility is unknown.

Local CZ-owned financial-services recruitment boutiques (as opposed to global brands) were not systematically enumerated in this pass — e.g. firms specialising in banking back-office, risk/compliance and insurance distribution recruitment.

LinkedIn is where CZ recruiters and headhunters post the most timely 'which functions are banks hiring' commentary and where leadership moves surface first, but it was not collected here and is login-walled.

Job-board demand data (LMC's Jobs.cz/Prace.cz reports, Profesia/Alma Career job-posting indices, Atmoskop employer reviews) was only touched at the edges; these give posting-volume time series per sector that lead recruiter guides.
Historical editions of the recruiter salary guides (needed to build multi-year banking pay and demand series) were only incidentally observed (one 2021 Hays PDF).
No URL in this slice was fetched; all entries rest on search-result evidence only, and several (Grafton 2026 page, Reed CZ guide, Finak article series) need liveness and cadence confirmation.

Career portals for several CZ banks and payment institutions were not located this pass: Fio banka, Banka CREDITAS, Trinity Bank, Max banka, Hello bank!, mBank CZ, plus non-bank PIs/EMIs (e.g. Global Payments, Worldline, ComGate, GoPay) and processing/ATM operators.
The canonical MPSV / Úřad práce integrated portal vacancy dataset was only reached via a third-party mirror (Kurzy.cz), not its official endpoint.

No ATS-layer sweep performed. Several fintechs publish only through ATS hosts (Recruitee confirmed for Twisto; Teamio, Greenhouse, Lever, Workable likely for others), which are usually more machine-readable than the boards.

Executive-search / headhunter sources for CZ banking leadership (e.g. specialised recruiters publishing mandates) were not explored; these are closer to the 'leadership moves' topic than volume job boards.
Job ads expire and are removed; no archival strategy identified, so historical hiring-burst baselines cannot be reconstructed retroactively.

Payments-sector actors (acquirers, PSPs, processors, card schemes, POS/ATM vendors operating in CZ — e.g. Global Payments CZ, Worldline, Monet+, ComGate, GoPay) have far thinner LinkedIn coverage in this slice than the retail banks; only scheme-side (Visa) and generic CEE profiles were captured.
No sanctioned, ToS-compliant mechanism has been identified for observing LinkedIn profile-headline changes over time, which is the single highest-value derivable signal in this cell.

Captured profiles skew to C-level and board tier. The cell's stated rationale is that mid-level and lateral moves are the bulk of org change, and those individuals are precisely the ones public search does not surface.

Czech-language querying was productive for appointment idioms ('jmenování ředitelem', 'nastupuji do', 'jsem hrdý') but was not extended to Slovak, despite heavy CZ/SK talent circulation in banking and payments and shared employers (Privatbanka, Vacuumlabs surfaced incidentally).

Because the direct channel (LinkedIn/X posts) is auth-walled, this slice is disproportionately dependent on indirect press mirrors, which lag the self-report by days to weeks and filter out non-senior moves.

Regulator-side registers that complement the commercial register were not covered here: ČNB's seznam regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů (list of banks, payment institutions, small-scale payment service providers, e-money issuers) and the ČNB fit-and-proper approvals of senior management.

CZ branches of foreign banks (odštěpný závod zahraniční osoby) and EU passported payment institutions have thin CZ register footprints; their real org changes are filed in the home-state register (e.g. AT, DE, SK) or the EBA register.

All findings in this slice come from search-result metadata and snippets; no page was fetched and parsed end-to-end, so schema details (ARES field names, dataor.justice.cz file structure, whether verejnerejstriky.msp.gov.cz exposes an API) remain unconfirmed.

The lag between a real leadership change and its register entry is not quantified. Law says 'bez zbytečného odkladu', but court processing adds weeks, and 'den vzniku funkce' can be backdated relative to 'zapsáno dne'.

English-language coverage of this cell is inherently thin — the primary sources are Czech-only, with only partial EN interfaces (verejnerejstriky.msp.gov.cz/en, ARES). No EN-language equivalent of the Sbírka listin exists.

Major commercial CZ corporate-data vendors were not surveyed: Cribis (CRIF), Dun & Bradstreet/Bisnode CZ, Albertina, and Rejstrik-Firem.cz. These typically offer the lowest-latency change alerts and cleaned person-entity resolution.

No listed-issuer disclosure channel exists for CZ payment institutions and fintechs (e.g. non-bank PSPs, e-money institutions) — none are PSE issuers, so MAR-driven leadership disclosure does not reach the payments half of the sector.

The Czech statutory corporate registry (obchodní rejstřík / sbírka listin at justice.cz), which records the legally effective appointment and removal of představenstvo and dozorčí rada members and holds AGM minutes, was not enumerated in this pass because it sits outside the 'regulated market disclosure' cell boundary.

Historical backfill of issuer announcements older than roughly a decade was not established; ČNB notes pre-31-July-2009 regulated information sits in a separate legacy database whose URL was not captured.

German-language ad-hoc disclosure by the Austrian parents (Erste, RBI, VIG) and Wiener Börse issuer news were not searched in German; the run's language scope is cs+en, but the legally binding ad-hoc text for these issuers is often German-first.
Feasibility of automated querying against ČNB CUri (form-based Oracle app) and of PDF parsing for AGM notices was not tested.
ČNOPK (German-Czech chamber) and British Chamber of Commerce CZ committee/board rosters not located; French, Nordic and Canadian chambers in CZ not searched at all.

Adjacent self-regulatory bodies not covered this pass: Česká asociace pojišťoven (ČAP), Asociace českých stavebních spořitelen (AČSS), Asociace penzijních společností ČR (APS ČR), and financial-intermediary bodies (USF ČR).
Several association sites appear JS-rendered (ČBA committees) or have entity-mangled deep links (AKAT), so static fetching under-collects.
No archival strategy identified for capturing historical board/member rosters, which is what makes a 'rotating leaderboard' analytically useful.
Associations were assessed as people/pointer sources; their own recruitment pages and members-only job boards (a direct jobs signal) were not investigated.
